|-----|------------------|---------------|-----|

| $08 | spriteset_shadow_aura_body ($97) | shad_sprites_1BC000 | Shadow's Aura body (SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08 in PlayerAuraTransformEntry); shares Shadow's tile graphics |

Rows 4-7 have a facing table each. FacingFormOffsetTable is indexed by $0AC8 - 4 and holds, in order, FacingData_WillAbilities (row 4, spriteset_will_abilities), FacingData_TransformPoses (row 5, spriteset_transform_poses), FacingData_FreedanFx (row 6, spriteset_freedan_fx) and FacingData_ShadowFx (row 7, spriteset_shadow_fx). With playerFlags bit 15 set, rows 0-3 fall back to FacingDirectionLookup. Row 8 is in neither group: $0AC8 = 8 gives index 8 - 4 = 4, which is not negative, so there is no fallback, and GetPlayerFacingDirection reads FacingFormOffsetTable + 8, past the 4-entry (8-byte) table; the word it reads there is the first two bytes of FacingData_WillAbilities, which follows the table directly. Not traced: whether GetPlayerFacingDirection runs while row 8 is active.

Selection by number: the only SetPlayerSpriteDirect operands in the scripts are 04, 05, 06 and 08 (24 sites). Row $07 is not selected by any of them. sE6_gaia is the only user of row $05. Row $08 is selected by SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08 in player_transition_handlers.PlayerAuraTransformEntry (item_use_system.UseItem_Aura, Shadow standing still). Nothing found selects row $03 by number (no SetPlayerSpriteDirect #03, and characterForm 3 is not traced), so what makes row $03 reachable is not traced.

cosine_table_16bit: 16-bit high-precision cosine table — 128 word entries covering one quarter-wave. Values range $7FFF (1.0) down to $0000 (0.0) (its entries are also the falling quarter, 90°–180°, of the sine cycle read from sine_table_16bit). Paired with sine_table_16bit for Mode 7 matrix computations in mode7_perspective.asm, which indexes it up to 512 words so the read continues through neg_sine_halfwave_16bit and cosine_table_16bit_tail.
cosine_table_16bit_tail: Copy of sine_table_16bit's 128 words (the rising quarter; entries $00–$09 and $70–$7F spot-checked identical). It follows neg_sine_halfwave_16bit so that the 512-word cosine cycle read from cosine_table_16bit ends with the 270°–360° quarter — it is not a spare duplicate. No code names it directly.

event_block_table: 158 entries of 8-byte event-block-def structs defining event-triggered tile copy operations. Fields: scene ID, source X/Y tile, width, height, dest X/Y tile, layer flag. Used for doors opening/closing, barriers appearing/disappearing, puzzle state changes. LookupEventBlock validates scene ID before execution (an entry whose scene differs from sceneCurrent is skipped); the rectangle is copied from the source to the destination coordinates. Coordinates and sizes are in 16×16 metatiles. Indexed by event_index × 8; the index comes from the COP event-block commands, an enemy's scene-record event byte (actor_execution) or an actor's deathActionIdx. Entry $07 is an all-zero 1×1 placeholder (scene 0); entries $06, $14 and $20 target layer 1 (layer flag 1), all others layer 0.

hdma_channel_config: DMAP transfer mode for each PPU B-bus register — 64 byte entries indexed by the register's low byte ($2100 + index; the HDMA COP ops pass that byte, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS, #26 = WH0). The low 3 bits are the DMAP transfer mode: 0 = one register, 1 = two registers (p, p+1), 2 = one register written twice. Matches the PPU map: 2 for the scroll registers $0D–$14, the mode 7 registers $1B–$20 and CGDATA $22, 1 for the VRAM address/data pairs $16–$19 and the window pairs $26–$29. The indirect-HDMA flag ($40) is not stored here; SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect and QueueHdmaChannel OR it in. Entries $34–$3F cover the read-only PPU registers (MPY, SLHV, OAMDATAREAD, VMDATAREAD, CGDATAREAD, OPHCT/OPVCT, STAT77/78) and carry bit 7 ($80/$81/$82), the DMAP PPU-to-CPU direction bit. Referenced by SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect/Direct in hdma_dma_spc.asm, QueueHdmaChannel in cop_handlers_hdma_dma.asm, and scanline_band_hdma_thinker.asm (which masks with AND #$07).
hdma_entry_stride_by_mode: HDMA entry stride (count byte + data bytes) indexed by the DMAP transfer mode: mode 0 = 2, modes 1 and 2 = 3. ParallaxResolveEntryStride (scanline_band_hdma_thinker) looks up hdma_channel_config[register index] & 7 and stores the result in DP $04, where the band writers use it to step the buffer write pointer. It is a stride, not a scroll speed. Only entries 00-02 ($02, $03, $03) are reachable because every config byte has a low-3-bit value of 0-2; entries 03-0C ($05, $05, $64, $00, then $FF / $7F pairs) have no reader (the FF 7F pattern resembles HDMA line-count data, inferred).

move_chain_00: Entry $00: value 0, link $0000 (null). ApplyMovement adds 0, stores $0000 in $2C / $2E and the actor falls back to its per-actor scratch delta. The only chain with a null link.
move_chain_01: Entries $01-$10 (01B134-01B170): one node each, linked to itself. $01 = +1, $02 = -1, $03 = +2, $04 = -2 ... $0F = +8, $10 = -8 pixels per frame.
move_chain_11: Entry $11: +1, 0 repeating (average +1/2 per frame). The next three entries are the same idea: $12 (01B17C) -1, 0; $13 (01B184) +1, 0, 0, 0 (+1/4); $14 (01B194) -1, 0, 0, 0 (-1/4). walk_step_table uses all four for the slow forced walks.
move_chain_15: Entry $15: -4 -4 -2 -2 -1 -1, four 0, +1 +1 +2 +2 +4 +4, then 0 held (17 nodes). A decelerating then accelerating swing: 14 pixels one way and back again, net 0.
move_chain_16: Entry $16: four +1 nodes in a cycle (the same motion as $01). Entry $17 (01B1F8) is the same with -1 (the same as $02).
move_chain_18: Entry $18: a 32-node closed loop: ten 0, -2 x3, -1 x4, eight 0, +1 x4, +2 x3 (net 0), the last node links back to the head, so the actor bobs out and back forever.
move_chain_22: Entry $22: 4 4 5 5 5 5 4 4 3 3 2 2 1 1 0 (15 nodes, 48 pixels, then 0 held). The tier 0 hit stagger knockback (hit_stagger_controller).
move_chain_23: Entry $23: 3 3 4 4 3 3 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 0 (15 nodes, 32 pixels, then 0 held). The hit stagger knockback for tier 1 and above, which includes the player.
move_chain_36: Entry $36: eight 0, then 4 4 7 7 9 9 12 12 (64 pixels out), 0 0, eight -8 (64 pixels back), then 0 held (27 nodes). An out-and-back curve; attack_ability_system names index $36 in its movement notes.
move_chain_3C: Entry $3C: +8, 0, 0, 0 repeating (4 nodes; average +2 per frame in jumps of 8 pixels). Entry $3F (01BC78) is +8, 0, 0 repeating (3 nodes).
move_chain_53: Entry $53: sixteen 0, then sixteen -1, and the last node links back to the head: -1 pixel per frame for 16 frames, still for 16, repeating.
move_chain_54: Entry $54, the last chain: sixteen 0, then the $15 swing (-4 -4 -2 -2 -1 -1, four 0, +1 +1 +2 +2 +4 +4), 32 nodes, the last node links back to the head: a periodic back-and-forth, net 0.
move_chain_table: 85 word pointers, indexed by the movement index ($00-$54), each the head of a delta-node chain. AnimFrameLookup returns table[index x 2]; callers store it in actor field $2C (X) or $2E (Y). See the block note for the node format, the chain endings and the index families.
music_pointer_array: 30 long-pointer entries covering 27 distinct BGM tracks (bgm_lively_city appears 4 times, at entries $00, $01, $0C, $16). Entry index = music ID - 1, so entry $1B (bgm_lively_city_by_the_sea) is music ID $1C, which matches the `music < #1C, ... @bgm_lively_city_by_the_sea >` scene records. The repeated lively_city entries sit at IDs $01, $02, $0D and $17; IDs $0D/$17 look like placeholders for unused IDs (inferred). The no-music track is entry $1A (ID $1B). Referenced by hdma_dma_spc.asm: LoadMusicFromTransitionState computes musicTransitionState x 3, reads the entry at `table-3 + index` into $46/$47 and the `srcCacheMusic` shadow ($0687/$0688), then calls SpcBlockTransfer.
neg_sine_halfwave_16bit: Negated half-wave 16-bit sine — 256 word entries, entry k ≈ −32767 × sin(k × 0.703125°): $0000 at k=0, trough $8001 at k=$80, back to $FE6E (−402) at k=$FF; never positive. It supplies angles 180°–360° of the 512-word sine cycle that follows sine_table_16bit and cosine_table_16bit, and the 90°–270° part of the cosine cycle read from cosine_table_16bit. Reached only by running past the end of those tables (mode7_perspective index up to 511); no code names it directly.
non_discardable_item_bits: 8 bytes $BC $FF $FF $FE $DF 0 0 0: one bit per item ID, set = cannot be discarded (byte = ID >> 3, bit = BitMaskTable[ID & 7]). Read by CheckItemDiscardable. Discardable: $00, $01, $06, $18, $25, $28-$3F.

ramp_curve_arc_32: Entry 1 of ramp_motion_curves: 32 signed Y deltas in pixels, -8 at the start, 0 at frames 15-17 and +8 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -50 (up) at frame 14; the sum is +8, so the player lands 8 pixels lower. Used by all other east/west ramps (spawn type 3).
ramp_curve_arc_64: Entry 0 of ramp_motion_curves: 64 signed Y deltas in pixels, one per frame, -16 at the start, 0 around frames 29-36 and +16 at the end. Cumulative rise peaks at -204 (up) at frame 28; the sum is 0. Used by the Itory ramp pair (spawn type 1).
ramp_motion_curves: Two arc entries (3 bytes each: curve address, frame count) used by RampArcDriver in ramps.asm. The ramp's arc child reads the player's statsPtr (0 or 1, set from the ramp's spawn type byte) x 3, then adds one sign-extended curve byte per frame to the PLAYER's Y ($16, confirmed: the child's $04 link is the spawner, the player). Values are pixel deltas. Entry 0: 64 frames, rises up to 204 pixels (frame 28) and returns, net 0. Entry 1: 32 frames, rises up to 50 pixels (frame 14), net +8 (ends 8 pixels lower). Both curves repeat most values twice in a row.

signed_cosine_table_8bit: Full-cycle signed 8-bit cosine table — 256 entries, entry k = round(127 × cos(k × 1.40625°)): $7F at k=0, $00 at k=$40, $81 (−127) at k=$80, $00 at k=$C0. Because it starts at the 90° peak it is also the continuation of sine_table_8bit (sine index k+64). Used as the second axis of orbital motion with sine_table_8bit (ApplyOrbitalOffsetXY, ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef, the incan ruins whirligig).
sine_table_16bit: 16-bit high-precision sine table — 128 word entries covering one quarter-wave (0°–90°, 0.703125° per step): entry k ≈ 32767 × sin(k × 0.703125°), $0000 to $7FFD. Used by the Mode 7 perspective system for rotation matrix calculations, which index it up to 512 words so the read continues through cosine_table_16bit and neg_sine_halfwave_16bit (see the block note).
sine_table_8bit: 8-bit sine lookup table — 64 entries covering one quarter-wave (0°–90°). Values range $00 to $7F. Entry i = round(127 × sin(i × 1.40625°)). Consumers index it with the full 0–255 range; entries 64–255 are read from the adjacent signed_cosine_table_8bit (see the block note). Used by actor code for circular/oscillating motion (whirligig, skulker, sand fanger spiral attacks) and by scene_lifecycle for the screen-transition sine-wave effect. Also used by system_init as a known zero-byte source address (entry 0) for WRAM DMA clearing.
slope_curve_table:
209-byte table at the start of the block. Despite its name it is not a scene-flag table: system_core's init code points slopeCurvePtrA/B ($09BA/$09BC) at its start and decelCurvePtr ($09C2, also $09BE/$09C0/$09C4) at +$20. slope_ramp_physics reads 16-bit values from those pointers indexed by (step counter & $0F) × 2, so the first 64 bytes are two 16-word curves:
- $00–$1F: default slope acceleration curve — word $0001 at steps 0, 4, 8 and 12, otherwise $0000.
- $20–$3F: default deceleration curve — word $0001 at steps 7 and 15, otherwise $0000.

The remaining bytes have no reference by name in the extracted code: $42–$C0 is a stepped ramp ($01 ×8, $02 ×8, … up to $10 ×7) and $C1–$D0 counts $E0–$EF. Their consumer is unknown (logged as an open question).
walk_step_table:
Step code -> (animation index, move_chain_table index). FacingDirectionLookup maps animation index 8 = down, 9 = up, 2 = left, 3 = right; move_chain_table index $11 / $12 / $13 / $14 = +1 / -1 / +1 / -1 on one frame in 2 / 2 / 4 / 4 (average +1/2, -1/2, +1/4, -1/4 pixel per frame, assuming one node per frame as ApplyMovement does).

| Code | Anim | Facing | Velocity chain |
|------|------|--------|----------------|
| $00 | 9 | up | $12 (-1/2 px per frame) |
| $01 | 8 | down | $11 (+1/2) |
| $02 | 9 | up | $14 (-1/4) |
| $03 | 8 | down | $11 (+1/2) |
| $04 | 9 | up | $14 (-1/4) |
| $05 | 9 | up | $12 (-1/2) |
| $06 | 2 | left | none ($00) |
| $07 | 3 | right | none ($00) |
| $08 | 8 | down | $13 (+1/4) |

Codes $00 = $05, $01 = $03 and $02 = $04 are identical rows. Left and right steps carry no velocity chain: the east and west forced-walk actors move through the camera pan (CameraPanRight and its mirror), not through this table. The vertical sign of every chain agrees with the facing (up = negative, down = positive).
